event_or_change: A veterans association and a military officers' wives club supported an early home for mixed-race children.
supported_observation: Military-community support and local child welfare were connected before ISS Okinawa's formation.
competing_reading: The arrangement may have been paternalistic relief, institutional necessity, or both.
claim_limit: Original governance and finance records are required before creating organization lineage or a funding edge.

event_or_change: OIWC's current application guide states that the organization was established in 1953.
supported_observation: A long-duration mixed-contact organization is publicly claimed.
competing_reading: Current continuity language may compress legal, membership or organizational changes.
claim_limit: Do not infer uninterrupted legal identity or exact historical member composition.

event_or_change: Official archive guide dates formation of International Social Service Okinawa to 1958.
supported_observation: A specialized welfare/casework institution addressed international family and child problems.
competing_reading: Formation date does not prove every predecessor relation described in secondary literature.
claim_limit: No actor ID or central genealogy edge is created.

event_or_change: Archive captions show selected Okinawan and American participants and a 1967 welfare bazaar for Wakaba Day Nursery.
supported_observation: Mixed participation and local welfare action are visible at event level.
competing_reading: USCAR publicity selection may overrepresent harmonious contact.
claim_limit: Event co-presence is not stable alliance, full membership census or legal continuity.

node_or_interface: Ryukyuan-American Welfare Council and nine affiliated clubs
event_or_change: Archive master caption names nine affiliated women's clubs and gift activity reaching Miyako and Yaeyama.
supported_observation: A pre-reversion umbrella coordinated a multi-club welfare interface beyond Okinawa Island.
competing_reading: Caption affiliation is a dated snapshot, not proof of predecessor/successor continuity.
claim_limit: Do not merge the council, clubs, OIWC or later AWWA from this caption alone.

event_or_change: A USMC compilation prepared in 2000 retrospectively states that AWWA was established in 1972 to coordinate six military spouses' groups' charitable contributions.
supported_observation: One official 2000 retrospective supplies a six-group account for the 1972 umbrella.
competing_reading: The source was compiled for public-affairs purposes and does not resolve relation to the Ryukyuan-American Welfare Council; five-, six- and seven-group counts in other descriptions remain unresolved.
claim_limit: Label this specifically as a 2000 official retrospective; do not encode a predecessor edge or freeze six groups across periods.

event_or_change: Archive guide records legal renaming to 社会福祉法人国際福祉沖縄事務所; secondary literature describes post-reversion transfer from American supporters toward Okinawan welfare professionals and public support.
supported_observation: Reversion coincided with organizational and support-structure change in this welfare interface.
competing_reading: This can be read as localization, administrative absorption, resource substitution, or institutional rupture.
claim_limit: Do not assume frictionless continuity or equate legal rename with unchanged governance.

event_or_change: The office issued 沖縄からの提言, including a nationality-law reform demand grounded in accumulated casework.
supported_observation: Care cases were aggregated and translated into a formal policy/rights claim.
competing_reading: The proposal may have been one input among broader legal and social campaigns.
claim_limit: The archive guide's later causal language is not causal identification.

event_or_change: Official archive guide records renaming to 社会福祉法人国際福祉会国際福祉相談所.
supported_observation: The office's legal/name trajectory is documentable.
competing_reading: A rename alone does not establish unchanged personnel, finance or practice.
claim_limit: Keep historical aliases time-bounded; no registry mutation in this package.

event_or_change: Archive guide retrospectively links the 1979 proposal to national-law reform.
supported_observation: The office's proposal preceded and addressed the problem later altered by law.
competing_reading: Law reform had multiple causes and broader national actors.
claim_limit: Use as a process lead, not as proof that one organization caused the reform.

event_or_change: The 2000 USMC compilation reports annual aggregate AWWA contributions to Japanese recipients, with one missing year, and identifies its spouse-group umbrella structure.
supported_observation: The service-side resource channel has documented multi-year depth before current web rosters.
competing_reading: Aggregates may reflect changing member clubs, accounting definitions and publicity selection.
claim_limit: No ultimate recipient table or central funding edge is inferred from annual aggregates.

event_or_change: A retrospective scholarly/public-history source reports Masayo Hirata's explicit statement that the base destroys life and that most cases derived from the base, while cooperation with U.S. military offices was sometimes necessary.
supported_observation: A welfare institution could both cooperate operationally with military offices and publicly name base responsibility.
competing_reading: This statement may represent a late-stage leadership articulation rather than every period of the organization.
claim_limit: Underlying speech/publication should be checked before report-level quotation or generalization.

event_or_change: Official archive guide records closure in 1998.
supported_observation: This specific institution ended; later similar work cannot be treated as automatic organizational continuation.
competing_reading: Functions and people may have dispersed to other institutions.
claim_limit: Closure does not imply that the social problem or all interface capacity disappeared.

node_or_interface: Amer-Asian School and U.S. Marine units
event_or_change: The USMC compilation says 3D FSSG units visited Amer-Asian School children and Headquarters and Service Battalion donated school materials.
supported_observation: A military-side material/contact interface remained publicly recorded after the consultation office closed.
competing_reading: The school is a different institution; the report's positive-program purpose may shape selection.
claim_limit: Do not assign actor IDs, create funding edges, or infer continuity from ISSO to the school.

event_or_change: Seven displayed cycles name 86 raw recipient rows/70 research keys, with strong child, disability and welfare emphasis.
supported_observation: A current mixed-contact organization also operates a recurring local-welfare resource interface.
competing_reading: Skipped years and count mismatch prevent full annual-network reconstruction.
claim_limit: Recipient status is not political alignment and roster recurrence is not a permanent partnership.

event_or_change: A third-party IRS-derived display contains four consecutive named filing-year rows for AWWA totaling $151,672.
supported_observation: The display supplies a recurrent filing-row candidate stronger than a one-off webpage mention.
competing_reading: Original filing pages are not yet checked; AWWA's ultimate allocations and MTS's smaller/unitemized endpoints remain unavailable.
claim_limit: All rows remain ai_seeded and require original-filing review before factual or central funding use.

node_or_interface: MTS, Lions conduit and local children's medical beneficiaries
event_or_change: DVIDS reports a $10,000 direct MTS donation routed through Lions, described as the first direct local-national donation bypassing the usual AWWA screen.
supported_observation: The normal intermediary gate can be bypassed through a specific institutional conduit.
competing_reading: The event may reflect exceptional access, publicity value, beneficiary urgency or all three.
claim_limit: Do not infer a general new policy or political stance from one official story.
